account: During 2023–24, as part of the DIII-D National Fusion Facility Program, Next Step Fusion applied reinforcement learning to control plasma parameters on the DIII-D tokamak. In its submission to the ITU AI for Good report of 2025, the company reports that this work also improved controller training. Next Step Fusion, General Atomics and UC San Diego authors published the DIII-D experiments in Nuclear Fusion on 21 January 2026. They report that four controllers trained in the NSFsim simulator ran in the DIII-D Plasma Control System and replaced its standard shape control, which relies on real-time equilibrium reconstruction. They report that the controllers kept shape errors within 1.5 to 2.0 cm and radial errors within 1 cm, with X-point errors of up to about 4 cm. The authors attribute the X-point error to mismatches between their simulator and the experiments. No independent source verifies these research results. Energy benefits remain prospective.

ai_role.statement: In the test discharges the RL controller replaced the standard shape-control category in the DIII-D Plasma Control System, so the reported shape errors reflect the trained policy. In some discharges the facility's fast vertical stability loop stayed on alongside it, and the authors attribute the X-point error to mismatches between their simulator and the experiments.
